info.title: CF Token Metadata Registry API
info.description: Query Cardano token metadata merged from CIP-26 and CIP-68, with additional script information for CIP-113 programmable tokens. V1 serves CIP-26 only and is retained here for existing integrations.

tags.name: V2 subjects
tags.description: Token metadata merged from CIP-26 and CIP-68, with separate CIP-113 extensions and validation errors.

tags.name: V1 (deprecated)
tags.description: CIP-26 metadata only, as served before V2. Use the V2 endpoints.

post.description: Query multiple properties of multiple subjects.

parameters.name: query_priority
parameters.description: the CIP priority: if the same property is present in multiple standards, the one with highest priority is returned

parameters.name: show_cips_details
parameters.description: whether all the CIP specific properties should be returned in the response. False by default

parameters.name: validation
parameters.description: which tokens to return, by how well their metadata follows its CIP: ALL (default) returns every indexed token with its validation_errors; MANDATORY_ONLY only tokens with no MANDATORY error; STRICT only tokens with no error at all (metadata.valid true). No error means none from the checks this API runs, not full CIP compliance: a CIP-68 text given as a list of byte strings is accepted, a URI is checked for its scheme only, and a CIP-26 logo for base64 and size, not for being a PNG (ADR-019). A token that is not accepted is left out of the response

post.description: Query either all or a subset of properties of the given subjects

get.description: Query all properties of the single subject specified by the given subject id.

get.summary: Get a property of a subject
get.description: Query a specific property of a single subject specified by the given subject id.

Query either all or a subset of properties of a given subject.

Returns the subject as indexed, with validation_errors saying how its metadata departs from its CIP. A subject is a 404 when nothing is indexed for it, or when the validation parameter does not accept it.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: the concatenation of policy id and asset name (if any) to query

parameters.name: property
parameters.description: the list of properties to be returned in the reponse, if none specified, all properties will be returned

parameters.name: query_priority
parameters.description: the CIP priority: if the same property is present in multiple standards, the one with highest priority is returned

parameters.name: show_cips_details
parameters.description: whether all the CIP specific properties should be returned in the response. False by default

parameters.name: validation
parameters.description: which tokens to return, by how well their metadata follows its CIP: ALL (default) returns every indexed token with its validation_errors; MANDATORY_ONLY only tokens with no MANDATORY error; STRICT only tokens with no error at all (metadata.valid true). No error means none from the checks this API runs, not full CIP compliance: a CIP-68 text given as a list of byte strings is accepted, a URI is checked for its scheme only, and a CIP-26 logo for base64 and size, not for being a PNG (ADR-019). A token that is not accepted is a 404

validation_errors.description: How the entry departs from CIP-26 (V2 only); empty when it follows it.

FungibleTokenMetadata.description: CIP-68 fungible (label 333) or rich fungible (label 444) token metadata from a reference NFT inline datum. The token is served as indexed, whatever is wrong with it: validation_errors lists how it departs from CIP-68.

logo.description: The logo as written, a URI with scheme https, ipfs, ar or data when it follows CIP-68. For a rich fungible token (444), which has no logo, this is its image.

validation_errors.description: How the datum departs from CIP-68 for this token's label; empty when it follows it, absent when the row was indexed before validation existed.

ProgrammableTokenCip113.description: CIP-113 programmable token metadata. Present when the token's policy ID is registered in an on-chain CIP-113 programmable token registry. CIP-113 tokens are standard CIP-26/CIP-68 tokens with additional on-chain transfer validation logic — effectively tokens in a 'smart contract jail' for regulatory compliance, freeze/seize, or custom rules.

minting_logic_script.description: Blake2b-224 hash of the minting logic credential (script or verification key) that authorises minting and burning of this token. Bound on-chain to the token's policy ID at registration. Null when the registry node does not specify one.

transfer_logic_script.description: Blake2b-224 hash of the Plutus script that validates every transfer of this token. This script runs on-chain via the withdraw-zero pattern whenever tokens move between addresses. Null when the registry node does not specify a transfer logic script.

third_party_transfer_logic_script.description: Blake2b-224 hash of the Plutus script that validates issuer/admin operations such as freeze, seize, or burn. Allows a token issuer to perform privileged actions on tokens held by other addresses. Null when the substandard has no third-party operations.

unfracking_logic_script.description: Blake2b-224 hash of the credential (script or verification key) that must approve any unfracking action touching this token. Null means unfracking is forbidden for this token.

global_state_policy_id.description: Policy ID of an optional global state NFT used by the transfer logic. For example, a freeze-and-seize substandard uses this to reference a denylist of blocked addresses. Null when the token's substandard has no global state.

Subject.description: A token subject with its metadata, standards details, and optional extensions from additional CIPs

subject.description: The subject identifier — concatenation of policy ID and asset name (hex)

type.description: Token type: NATIVE for standard tokens, PROGRAMMABLE for tokens with on-chain transfer logic (e.g. CIP-113)

metadata.description: Merged display metadata from CIP-26/CIP-68 based on query priority

standards.description: Raw per-standard metadata when show_cips_details=true, null otherwise

extensions.description: Additional on-chain properties from CIP extensions. Each key is a CIP identifier (e.g. 'cip113'). Omitted when the token has no extensions.

validation_errors.description:
How the metadata of the token departs from its CIP, from every standard that has it, in query priority order (each entry names its cip and, for CIP-68, its sub_standard, the label). The token is returned as indexed; a MANDATORY error means it lacks something its CIP requires, so a wallet that wants to be strict may reject it, or ask with validation=MANDATORY_ONLY. Absent when the token was indexed before validation existed; metadata.valid then falls back to name and description being present.

| code | meaning |
|---|---|
| `missing_value` | a field the CIP requires is missing or empty: for CIP-68 the `version` and, as the label requires it, `name`, `description` (333) and `image` (222, 444); for CIP-26 `name` and `description`; for CIP-113 the CIP-26 or CIP-68 metadata of a programmable token (`companion_metadata`) |
| `wrong_type` | the value has a type the CIP does not allow (for example a number where text is expected); a value that cannot be kept is left out |
| `invalid_uri_scheme` | an `image` or `logo` is not a URI with one of the schemes CIP-68 allows (`https`, `ipfs`, `ar`, `data`); the value is kept as written |
| `invalid_length` | a CIP-26 text is shorter or longer than CIP-26 allows (for example a `name` over 50 characters) |
| `invalid_value` | a CIP-26 value breaks a rule of the registry's validator that is not a type, a length or a range |
| `out_of_range` | a number is outside the range allowed: `decimals` |
| `invalid_version` | the CIP-68 `version` is there but cannot be used: it is not an integer, it does not fit a 64-bit integer (stored without a version), or it is not one CIP-68 defines (1 to 4; the datum is read by its structure and kept). The message says which. A missing `version` is `missing_value` |
| `plutus_constructor` | a property holds a Plutus constructor, which CIP-68 metadata does not allow; it is kept as `{constructor, fields}` |
| `not_utf8` | a text is not valid UTF-8; it is kept as hex (mandatory for a `name`, and for the `description` of a 333) |
| `invalid_files_entry` | an entry of `files` breaks the CIP-68 definition (for example no `mediaType` or `src`); the entry is kept |
| `no_nested_entry` | a nested datum (`"721"`) has no usable entry for the token (field `721`); the token is indexed without metadata |
| `too_deep` | a property is nested more than 100 levels and is dropped, the rest of the datum is kept |
| `unsupported_key` | a key of a map has no text form (a list or a map) and is left out |
| `key_collision` | two keys read the same (for example the text `1` and the integer `1`); one of them is kept |
| `invalid_base64` | a CIP-26 `logo` is not valid base64 |
| `too_large` | a CIP-26 `logo` is over 64 KiB once decoded (kept up to about 1 MiB; anything larger is dropped) |
| `invalid_constructor` | the CIP-68 datum is not constructor 0 (`#6.121`), as CIP-68 defines it (field `constructor`); it is read as written |

SubjectBatchResponse.description: The subjects found, in the order asked, and the query priority used
